title: Keep the keyboard backlight level across lock and suspend
author: mohan314e
body:
## What's wrong

The keyboard backlight goes off and never comes back. Turning it on by hand doesn't help — the next wake turns it off again.

## How it's meant to work

Locking blanks the backlight:

1. Remember the current level (`brightnessctl -s`)
2. Set it to 0

Waking puts it back:

3. Restore the remembered level (`brightnessctl -r`)

That is correct, as long as step 1 only ever runs while the light is actually on.

## Why it breaks

Step 1 remembers **whatever it finds** — including 0. So a blank that runs while the light is already off remembers 0.

After that, "restore the remembered level" means "set it to 0". Every time. Nothing ever writes a good value back, so it never heals on its own.

So the whole bug reduces to one question: **can a blank ever run while the light is already off?**

## Yes — and only one path does it

A blank is normally preceded by a wake, and a wake restores the light. So the light is on when the blank runs. Fine.

Four places schedule a blank:

| | what it is | wake before it? |
|---|---|---|
| `:146` | you lock the screen | yes — you were just using the laptop |
| `:181` | you touch the lock screen | yes — `runWake()` ran first |
| `:551` | a password attempt ends | yes — submitting called `runWake()` |
| `:490` | **resume from suspend** | **no** |

`:490` is the suspend gap. The blank countdown freezes during suspend. On resume it fires late, notices the gap, and re-arms — but it never wakes anything:

1. Before suspend: blank runs. Remembers 40, sets 0.
2. Suspend, then resume. The light is still 0.
3. `:490` fires and re-arms. No wake, so nothing restores the light.
4. Five seconds later the blank runs again. It finds 0. **It remembers 0.**

Poisoned, permanently.

Resume can't be rescued anywhere else either. `runWake()`'s callers are `:169`, `:218`, `:244`, `:298` and `:323`, and the last needs real typing or mouse movement on the lock screen. Opening a lid is neither.

**Fix 1 — `Service.qml:490`: wake, don't just re-arm.** `runWake()` arms the timer itself while locked, so the five-second run-up before blanking still happens. The light is simply real again before the next blank records it.

## A second, separate problem

Restore writes the remembered level no matter what. But the backlight hotkeys still work while locked. So if you set the level yourself on the lock screen, the next wake throws your choice away (#10767).

The level at restore time tells you which happened:

| level when restore runs | what it means | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| still 0 | nothing has touched it since the blank | the remembered level is still yours — apply it |
| anything else | it was set *after* the blank | that is newer than what we remembered — leave it alone |

The same rule also covers locking while the light was already off: remembers 0, sees 0, applies 0 — no change, no special case needed.

**Fix 2 — `restore` only writes while the level is still 0.**

This is also why `off` is left as-is. Guarding `off` against saving 0 would mean a backlight you deliberately turned off is never remembered, and the next wake would switch it back on.

**Fix 3 — `omarchy-system-wake` restores the keyboard before the display.** The display call goes through Hyprland IPC, which lid transitions can stall; the keyboard write goes straight to sysfs and is instant. Doing it first means it is already done if the display call hangs — and `runWake()` drops a new wake request while the previous one is still running.

`OMARCHY_LEDS_PATH` follows the existing `OMARCHY_BACKLIGHT_PATH` and `OMARCHY_DRM_PATH` seams, so the new test can run on hardware with no keyboard backlight.

Reported in #9339, #10105 and #7650.

**Validation:** the new `test/shell.d/brightness-keyboard-test.sh` covers blank/restore, a level changed while blanked, and a deliberate zero. It fails against the unpatched script and passes on this branch. `qmllint` reports no new warnings on `Service.qml`. `./test/all` passes apart from ten files that fail identically on a clean checkout in this environment for unrelated reasons. The three changes were also applied to a running 4.0.4-1 system and exercised through real blank and restore cycles; a full suspend and resume cycle was not manually tested.
